title: The show bus and advertising through town
summary: Moon's custom bus had bunks and a rear platform where the band played to advertise the evening show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: guy who played a baritone horn -- not a saxophone; it was a baritone horn. So he wanted me to play saxophone. At that time, he had a bus that was made special, that cost thirty thousand dollars, in 19...this was the early part of '25.

That's right. And he had little bunks where you could sleep, and he had a fairly good room on it for himself, where him and his wife slept in, and they had a little old stove there. They had a guy cooking, that would double on helping them put up a portable platform stage.
And they'd work off the back of the bus...

No, we didn't work on it. We used the back of the bus... They had a little observation platform like you see on Pullman cars on the railroad. Well, naturally, it wasn't that big. But that was used when we drove through town to advertise.
You'd drive through town in a bus.

Playing on the back of a bus with a sign painted on some kind of a paper banner or something, and stuff on the side of bus: "The Show Will Be At Such-and-Such A Street, on Elman and Cherry Street Tonight at Eight O'clock." Usually, that's the time they started. One hour.
